name: Xteink X4
description: 4.26 inch monochrome ePaper e-reader, ESP32-C3, 800x480 panel mounted portrait (480x800 presentation). Two firmware paths speak Tesserae's v1 REST device API: CrossInk with Tesserae client support, which paints the dashboard as the reader's sleep screen on an explicit sleep transition (the radio never comes up on a timer), and the native Tesserae device firmware (`xteink-x4`), which polls on the normal deep-sleep cadence with the power button advancing the rotation. Server-side pack via esp32_bw_bin produces a raw 1-bpp mono buffer (48000 bytes) painted with no on-device decode; both firmwares consume identical bytes.
notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware (GDEQ0426T82 / SSD1677) on both firmware paths: CrossInk 1.4.0 with Tesserae client support, and the native Tesserae device firmware (tesserae-device-firmware env `xteink-x4`).

Wire format is exactly 48000 bytes (800*480/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum, identical to seeed_reterminal_e1001 and xiao_epaper_75.

Orientation is the ordinary presentational setting and the two firmwares agree on it: the same registration (`portrait_flipped`, this entry's default) has painted upright on both CrossInk and the native firmware on the same unit, so no per-firmware value is needed. Pick the orientation matching the physical mounting, as on any panel. Historical diagnosis note: plain `portrait` painted 180 degrees out (readable, rotated, no mirror), first isolated by registering the unit against the landscape `xiao_epaper_75` kind, hence the flipped default for a reader stood upright.

Xteink shipped a second panel revision mid-production (SSD1677 -> UC8179; later runs also UC8279). CrossInk detects the controller at boot and both revisions consume the same buffer, so no separate SKU is needed there. The native Tesserae firmware is an SSD1677-only build: a UC8179/UC8279 unit will not refresh on it at all and needs a firmware target of its own.

See `xteink_x4_gray` for the 4-level grayscale variant of the same panel (CrossInk only; the native firmware runs the panel in mono).
